syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Relations as subsets; empty and universal relations

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a relation in a set A as a subset of A x A and count the relations on a finite set.
Identify empty and universal (trivial) relations in a given set.
Test whether a given relation is reflexive.
Test whether a given relation is symmetric.
Test whether a given relation is transitive and find pairs needed for transitivity.
Decide whether a relation is an equivalence relation by checking all three properties.
Find the equivalence class of an element under a given equivalence relation.
Determine whether a function is one-one (injective) or many-one.
Determine whether a function is onto (surjective) for a given co-domain.

topics.title: Bijective functions and functions on finite sets

concepts.learning_objective: Prove that a function is bijective and count bijections between finite sets.
Use the fact that for a finite set X, f : X -> X is one-one if and only if it is onto.

topics.title: Restricting domains: principal branches of sin⁻¹ and cos⁻¹

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a trigonometric function must be restricted to an interval on which it is one-one and onto before it can be inverted.
State the domain and principal value range of sin⁻¹.
State the domain and principal value range of cos⁻¹ and identify valid branches.

topics.title: Principal branches of cosec⁻¹, sec⁻¹, tan⁻¹ and cot⁻¹

concepts.learning_objective: State the domains and principal value ranges of cosec⁻¹ and sec⁻¹ and explain the excluded values.
State the domains and principal value ranges of tan⁻¹ and cot⁻¹.
Find principal values of inverse trigonometric functions and evaluate expressions built from them.
Distinguish sin⁻¹ x from (sin x)⁻¹ and obtain the graph of an inverse function by reflection in the line y = x.

topics.title: Composition properties of inverse trigonometric functions

concepts.learning_objective: Use sin(sin⁻¹ x) = x and sin⁻¹(sin x) = x with their conditions on x.
Evaluate expressions such as sin⁻¹(sin θ) when θ lies outside the principal branch.

topics.title: Writing inverse trigonometric expressions in the simplest form

concepts.learning_objective: Choose a suitable substitution such as x = sin θ, x = a sin θ or x = sec θ to simplify an inverse trigonometric expression.
Simplify expressions in cos x and sin x using half-angle identities to reach tan⁻¹(tan θ).
Identify the order of a matrix and locate its element a_ij by row and column.
Construct a matrix whose elements are given by a rule in i and j, and list the possible orders for a given number of elements.
Classify matrices as row, column, square, diagonal, scalar, identity or zero matrices.
Use the conditions for equality of matrices to find unknown elements.
Add and subtract matrices of the same order and apply the properties of matrix addition.
Multiply a matrix by a scalar and solve simple matrix equations using these operations.
Decide when a product of matrices is defined, find its order and compute it.
Apply the properties of matrix multiplication, including non-commutativity and zero products of non-zero matrices.

topics.title: Transpose, symmetric and skew symmetric matrices

concepts.learning_objective: Find the transpose of a matrix and apply the properties of transpose, including (AB)' = B'A'.
Identify symmetric and skew symmetric matrices and express a square matrix as their sum.
Use the definition AB = BA = I to recognise and verify the inverse of a square matrix.
Apply the uniqueness of the inverse and the result (AB)^(-1) = B^(-1)A^(-1).
Evaluate determinants of order 1, 2 and 3 by expanding along a row or a column.
Use |kA| = k^n |A| for a square matrix A of order n.
Find the area of a triangle, or an unknown vertex coordinate, using a determinant.
Use a zero determinant to test collinearity and find the equation of a line through two points.
Find the minor Mij and the cofactor Aij = (-1)^(i+j) Mij of an element.
Express a determinant as the sum of products of a row's elements with their cofactors.

topics.title: Adjoint and inverse of a matrix

concepts.learning_objective: Find the adjoint of a square matrix and use A(adj A) = (adj A)A = |A| I.
Classify a matrix as singular or non-singular and relate this to invertibility.
Find the inverse of a non-singular matrix using A^(-1) = (1/|A|) adj A.
Decide whether a system AX = B is consistent using |A| and (adj A)B.
Solve a system of linear equations in two or three variables using X = A^(-1) B.

topics.title: Continuity of a function at a point and on its domain

concepts.learning_objective: Use the condition lim f(x) as x tends to c equals f(c) to decide whether a function is continuous at c.
Find unknown constants and points of discontinuity of piecewise-defined functions using one-sided limits.
Apply the sum, difference, product and quotient results for continuous functions, including polynomial and rational functions.
Use the theorem that a composite of continuous functions is continuous.

topics.title: Differentiability and its relation with continuity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that every differentiable function is continuous but a continuous function need not be differentiable.
Compute left-hand and right-hand derivatives to test differentiability at a point.

topics.title: Derivatives of composite and implicit functions

concepts.learning_objective: Differentiate composite functions using the chain rule.
Find dy/dx when x and y are related implicitly by an equation.
Recall and apply the derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions in their domains.
Simplify inverse trigonometric expressions by a suitable substitution before differentiating.
Differentiate functions involving e^x using the chain rule.
State the domain of log x and differentiate functions involving the natural logarithm.
Differentiate functions of the form [u(x)]^v(x) by taking logarithms.
Use logarithms to differentiate products and quotients of several factors.

topics.title: Parametric forms and second order derivatives

concepts.learning_objective: Find dy/dx when x and y are given in terms of a parameter.
Find second order derivatives and verify relations involving them.
Interpret dy/dx as the rate of change of y with respect to x and evaluate it at a given point.
Use the chain rule to relate rates of change of quantities that vary with time.
Find marginal cost and marginal revenue as derivatives of total cost and total revenue.
State the definitions of increasing, decreasing, strictly increasing and strictly decreasing functions on an interval.
Use the sign of f′(x) on an interval to decide whether f is strictly increasing, strictly decreasing or constant.
Find the intervals in which a function is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing using its critical points.

topics.title: Maximum and minimum values and critical points

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the maximum, minimum and extreme values of a function on an interval.
Find the critical points of a function and recognise that f′(c) = 0 is necessary but not sufficient for a local extremum.
Classify a critical point using the change in sign of f′(x) as x increases through it.
Classify a critical point using the sign of f″(c) and recognise when the test fails.

topics.title: Absolute maximum and minimum on a closed interval

concepts.learning_objective: State that a continuous function on a closed interval attains an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum.
Find absolute maximum and minimum values by comparing f at the critical points and the end points.

topics.title: Applied problems on maxima and minima

concepts.learning_objective: Model number and mensuration situations as functions and find their maximum or minimum values.
Solve real-life optimisation problems such as maximum volume and maximum revenue.
